summary.oneLiner: A debt-free, cash-rich (INR 25 bn) grid-equipment leader riding India's multi-year T&D + HVDC super-cycle, with record 27.2% Q4 EBITDA margin, INR 214.6 bn backlog (+49% YoY) and optionality from HVDC (LCC + first-ever VSC win), exports, and data centres.

one-line thesis: A debt-free, cash-rich (INR 25 bn) grid-equipment leader riding India's multi-year T&D + HVDC super-cycle, with record 27.2% Q4 EBITDA margin, INR 214.6 bn backlog (+49% YoY) and optionality from HVDC (LCC + first-ever VSC win), exports, and data centres.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 (full) | FY25 (full) | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Order intake | INR 86.1 bn | INR 29.9 bn | +188% | INR 147.76 bn | INR 107.0 bn | +37% |
| Revenue | INR 16.4 bn | INR 11.4 bn | +42% | INR 62.1 bn | INR 42.9 bn | +45% |
| EBITDA / margin | margin 27.2% (record) | — | — | INR 17 bn | INR 8 bn | >2x |
| PBT (pre-exceptional) | INR 4.6 bn | INR 2.6 bn | ~1.8x | INR 17.1 bn | INR 8.2 bn | 2.1x |
| Order backlog | INR 214.6 bn | INR 143.8 bn | +49% (~+70% over 12m) | — | — | — |
| Cash & equiv. | INR 25.0 bn | INR 10.5 bn | — | (FCF gen FY26 INR 15.8 bn; Q4 INR 9 bn) | — | — |

**One-offs:** FY26 exceptional charge INR 690 mn (one-time, non-operational provision for retirement benefit obligation under new Wage Code); INR 57 mn reversal in Q4. Q4 other expenses included ~INR 500 mn (INR 50 cr) notional MTM loss on FX derivatives — excluding it, Q4 EBITDA margin would have been even higher. Debt: INR 0. Dividend: INR 10/share recommended for FY26.
guidance (next quarter / forward):
- **Margins:** Endeavour to hold **mid-20s%** going forward, with upside from productivity/cost actions (started FY26 guiding low-20s, revised up twice to high-20s).
- **Revenue:** Will keep growing; rate varies by year. Long-cycle HVDC projects convert meaningfully **FY28-29 onwards**.
- **Base order intake:** Confident of **INR 70 bn (INR 7,000 cr) base orders** in FY27; not seeing substantial pipeline growth but a consistent pipeline.
- **Exports:** A single RPT export order (~INR 14–15 bn) expected to close in **Q1 FY27** could alone exceed all of FY26 exports; US data-center product RPT order expected to be decided **current quarter**; UK Grid Solutions order (buy-side, feeds Adani HVDC) also expected current quarter.
- **STATCOM:** Awards expected to improve in FY27 vs FY26.
order book & pipeline:
- Backlog INR 214.6 bn; **98%** from private/central utilities/PSUs; **state-utility exposure <2%** (all-time low). FY26 new bookings ~92% domestic.
- Q4 intake INR 86.1 bn includes the **first-ever VSC HVDC order (Adani, Khavda-Olpad)** — value undisclosed (customer confidentiality). Localization requirement = 0 for that VSC project.
- HVDC pipeline: only **Barmer** tender currently live (LCC, getting extended); other listed LCC projects — **South Kalamb, Lakadia-Alephata, Pusauli upgradation**. ~10 Rajasthan HVDC projects targeted by 2035-36 (~1/yr cadence, possibly more incl. Brahmaputra Basin / private city in-feed).
- TBCB: ~**33 packages under decision**, of which 21 are 765 kV.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- Managed as **one integrated portfolio** — no segment/product-vs-project/export-vs-domestic split disclosed.
- Q4 commissioning highlights: Gadag substation (ReNew, 400/220 kV AIS); PGCIL Nagaland 132 kV GIS; NTPC Kahalgaon 400 kV AIS + 400 MVA transformers; HPPTCL Kangoo; PGCIL Ramgarh 765 kV shunt reactors + 765 kV ICTs; Sterlite Kishtwar; PGCIL Maheshwaram & Bhadla-III; Godrej & IIT Mumbai GIS.
- Grid automation/software: prior large orders were **software** (network level); one software tender live; wide-area monitoring (WAMS) opportunities ahead. Software done from India for India only (global platform).
- Out of scope (separate GE Vernova legal entities): synchronous condensers, nuclear (Hitachi JV), power generation, on-site engineering COE for global HVDC.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **HVDC** — biggest driver; even 30% back-end execution of a >$1 bn project = INR 30–50 bn/yr. LCC→LCC and LCC→VSC refurbishment pipeline (20-25-yr-old assets).
- **Exports** — ~30% of FY26 revenue; from Indian factory ("India for the World"); products reach 60+ countries; US/Europe/Middle East/Australia all in up-cycle simultaneously (unlike last India-only cycle).
- **Data centres** — India installed only ~1.5 GW (mostly 220 kV) → insignificant backlog today; expected to grow to 6–10 GW in 5-7 yrs and move to 400/765 kV. US data-center product export the bigger near-term opportunity. Data centres give better price realization than UMPP power.
- **Disconnectors & drives** — restarting (was discontinued at Padappai); demand returning; new Vallam (Tamil Nadu) facility, also a potential global feeder factory.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Record Q4 EBITDA margin 27.2% driven by: higher export share, favourable mix (export + high-value services), roll-off of low-priced legacy contracts, shift to central/private customers, lean/productivity gains.
- RM pass-through: transformers (standalone or within HVDC) have **price-escalation clauses**; other products carry inflation estimates baked into tender cost to protect margins.
- Royalty/group charges to parent: ~INR 1.9 bn FY26 (~3% of revenue) vs ~INR 1.4 bn FY25 (~3.3%) — revenue-linked formula (tech license + trademark + HQ charges; data management is separate opex).
capex / expansion:
- FY26: initiated **>INR 10 bn (INR 1,000 cr)** capex across multiple product lines/facilities; phased from start FY27 to end FY28; self-funded (split FY27/FY28 not disclosed).
- New Board approval (post Q4): **INR 550 mn (INR 55 cr)** for disconnectors + drives (for tank circuit breakers) at new **Vallam, Tamil Nadu** facility.
- Also adding thyristor valve & controls facility (for HVDC, fully India-made end product) and an **air-core reactor** facility — driving HVDC local content sharply higher (vs ~one-third transformers allowed in 2012-era orders → now 100% transformers from India).
capital allocation:
- INR 0 debt, ~INR 25 bn cash surplus; FY26 FCF INR 15.8 bn. Self-funding >INR 10 bn capex program.
- Dividend INR 10/share recommended (FY26). Policy: balance growth investment with constant dividend.
- No distribution-transformer entry in India (US Prolec strategy not replicable here — uneconomic to import; would need organic/inorganic build, low-value-add margins).
risks & watch-items:
- **Order lumpiness:** Q4 domestic intake admittedly "dull" (conscious selective decision); intake best viewed annually not quarterly.
- **HVDC revenue back-ended** to FY28-29 — long gap before VSC/Adani order converts.
- **Export RPT timing:** flagship RPT export order delayed (now expected H2 FY27); execution skew to FY27 closures.
- VSC localization limited — control-panel hardware still imported (no India supply chain yet).
- TBCB ordering slowdown in FY26 (PGCIL order book flattening); no substantial pipeline growth expected FY27.
- Margin sustainability if legacy roll-off benefit and export mix normalize (guidance prudently set at mid-20s vs 27% delivered).
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, candid. Clear on what they will not disclose (order values, segment splits, project phasing) and consistently steers to annual framing. Margin guidance repeatedly beaten (low-20s → high-20s) yet kept conservative. Strong de-risking narrative (state exposure <2%, zero debt). Credible on long-cycle structural story; avoids hype on data centres while keeping optionality open.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The UK Grid Solutions RPT is a **buy-side** (purchase) order feeding the Adani HVDC — full revenue still flows through the Indian listco; backlog/margins captured in India.
- This is GVTD's **first-ever US order** (HV products for US data centres) — a structurally new geography opening despite parent's Prolec presence.
- HVDC localization economics transformed: 2012-era orders allowed only ~1/3 transformers from India; new orders 100% transformers + valves/controls/air-core reactors India-made — large value-capture uplift.
- Data centres prized less for volume than for **price realization** — higher margin per unit vs conventional generation evacuation.
- Capacity ≠ revenue ceiling: HVDC revenue leverages manpower + bought-out equipment, not just in-house plant — apply asset-turnover, not nameplate, for top-line modelling.

| India T&D / HVDC super-cycle (NEP 500 GW under implementation + 400 GW to 2035) | GVTD · 522275 (self) | — | Record INR 214.6 bn backlog, HVDC + 765 kV pipeline; High |

| First VSC HVDC adoption (Adani Khavda-Olpad) | GVTD · 522275 (self) | — | First-mover VSC win, builds India control platform; Med-High |

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.
